extracted.intended_audience: educated readers of natural philosophy and natural theology (18th-century learned public)
extracted.subtask_description: Expository natural-philosophy / natural-theology text arguing from observed properties of matter (smallness, laws, cohesion, attraction, etc.) to conclusions about order/design. The excerpt treats definitions of laws of nature and several specific 'powers' (cohesion, separation, percussion, attraction) with experimental and quantitative examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conviftions from the Smalneſs of the Particles (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Argument that the innumerable multitude and extreme smallness of particles composing visible things (water, air, fire, scent particles, etc.) serve as evidence of order and direction rather than blind chance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides experimental/observational examples (benjoin smoke filling a chamber, scent particles from musk/civet, particles from lodestone passing through glass, mites visible under microscopes, counts of particles of light vs hairs) to show both immense number and determinate behaviour of particles; used to conclude that such regularity and operation 'cannot have been produced without any Order' and thus point to a directing Wisdom. Emphasises both quantity (huge numbers; arithmetical comparisons) and qualitative determinateness (retention of scent, function).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sect. I. What a Law.of Nature is.
rubrics_metrics.description: A law of nature is defined as 'a kind of Power producing something in or about Bodies or their Parts, and which may be experimentally proved in certain Circumstances to have always place in the same.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The text treats this as an operational/experimental definition; it explicitly disclaims metaphysical origin (first cause vs intermediate causes) and frames laws as repeatable powers demonstrable by experiment. Use this definition when judging whether a regularity counts as a 'law'.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Laus and Powers of Coheſion
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohesion is the power whereby certain determinate kinds of atoms are fasten'd to each other to produce determinate particular effects; observed in the stability and hardness of bodies like flints, iron, diamonds, and in the different cohesion appropriate to different tissues (teeth vs tongue).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence comes from experiments (Marriotte, Huygens) showing bodies resist separation and do not behave like loose dust; the variety of cohesion (hardness/softness) is argued to be adapted to function (teeth must be hard, tongue soft). Use contrasts and experimental demonstrations of required violence to separate parts as proof of cohesive power. The variety and appropriateness of cohesion is treated as evidence of wisdom in design.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Laws and Powers of Separation
rubrics_metrics.description: There exist laws/powers that separate particles which had cohered, enabling processes like fermentation, putrefaction, and the recycling of matter into new useful forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separation is presented as necessary to prevent the world being clogged with dead matter; it allows formation of fertile earth and other beneficial transformations. Use examples of fermentation/putrefaction and the cyclical re-formation of matter to demonstrate the constructive role of separation laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Unattrition of ſuch fine and tender Particles
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an observed law/power that the very fine particles of matter, despite innumerable motions, frictions, and collisions over ages, continue without being worn away (do not trivially grind to rounded atoms); their persistence of form is remarkable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that despite perpetual collisions (air, fire, water particles striking each other and hard bodies), particles retain necessary forms; this persistence (unattrition) is invoked as another law that preserves the order of the universe and supports the inference of design. Use as a criterion when assessing claims about the permanence or stability of microscopic constituents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two Principal Laus of Nature: Percuſſion and Attraction (with Repulſion)
rubrics_metrics.description: The text identifies two principal powers observed in bodies' motions: Percussion (impacts/striking) and Attraction (termed by mathematicians; often accompanied by Repulsion). Percussion describes collisions and transfer/augmentation of velocity and force; Attraction/Repulsion describes bodies moving toward or away from others without intervening bodies (e.g., gravity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Percussion: cites experiments and paradoxes (Marriotte, Huygens) showing that a chain of bodies can amplify velocity and force enormously; uses these facts to show strict mathematical regularities in impacts. Attraction/Repulsion: defined by movement toward/from without proximate protrusion; gravitational motions of planets and satellites are cited as phenomena with no fully understood mechanical protruding cause. The incomprehensibility of mechanism is used to support the inference to a superior Direction. When evaluating physical claims, give weight to experimentally demonstrable rules of percussion and the observed regularity of attraction (gravity), even if mechanisms remain obscure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conviftions from the Smallneſs of the Particles of Fire and Light (optical laws)
rubrics_metrics.description: Small particles of fire and light behave according to very strict optical laws; experiments (candle flame particle counts, Newton's Opticks) show vast numbers of light/fi re particles governed by exact laws of optics and prevented from producing global combustion by restraining laws.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uses quantitative examples (extremely large counts of particles emitted by a candle per second) and appeals to optical experiments to argue each particle is 'so strictly bound to certain Laws' that their behaviour is highly ordered; Newton is cited. Treat optical regularity and exact mathematical laws governing light as independent evidence of order requiring explanation beyond chance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Great Bodies are for the most part divided at firſt into ſmall Particles (divisibility for utility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Large consolidated bodies must be divided into small particles before they become useful as water, fire, or combustibles (examples: ice vs fluid water, fuels producing flame when their particles are set free, gunpowder's action when particles are released).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argument shows divine economy in making use of divisibility: the utility of substances (navigation, rain, nourishment, combustion) depends on their being separable into innumerable small particles. Use observations of phase-change, combustion, distillation, and gunpowder to evaluate claims about functional roles of divisibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Order, Regularity, and Variety of physical laws as evidence of Direction/Wisdom
rubrics_metrics.description: Because innumerable particles obey strict mathematical rules, exhibit appropriate variety (hardness vs softness, suitable cohesion), and perform coordinated operations, the reasonable conclusion is that a directing Wisdom (Divine Providence) governs them rather than blind chance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the overarching argumentative criterion: putative laws' precision, ubiquity, suitability to ends, and often the incomprehensibility of their underlying 'how' are all taken together as signs warranting belief in a wise Director. The text repeatedly invites the sceptic to consider the numerical magnitude, regularity, and adaptiveness of phenomena as grounds for this inference.
